candidate_proposition: If a provider optimizes completed tasks while charging human exception work outside its task metric, policies that create avoidable exception work can make wider permission rational for the user even when a narrower policy has the same completion quality.
strongest_interpretation: Holding successful task output and inherent approval requirements fixed, a policy that shifts coordination work to the user can increase rational additional delegation. Test whether charging that work to provider performance changes policy selection without rewarding permission directly.

KNOWN: Unmeasured effort, burden-driven delegation, truthful influence and instrumental control are inherited. Formal scope changes can be treated as intermediate states in existing incentive models.
NEW_RESIDUE: A workflow benchmark that matches task quality and distinguishes intrinsic from induced user exception work.
so_what_prior_theory_misses: A task-only product evaluation misses induced coordination cost; a researcher already combining multitask incentives with endogenous delegation need not make a new conceptual error.
verdict: Demote as a benchmark extension. No strong theoretical novelty residue is established; generic authority acquisition does not rescue it.
absence_claim: No absence-of-prior-work proof. Partial inspection cannot show that an entire work lacks an extension.
